newsitem.title: USA: NCAA-BOSTON COLLEGE COMMITTEE PROBING POSSIBLE FOOTBALL GAMBLING.
newsitem.headline: NCAA-BOSTON COLLEGE COMMITTEE PROBING POSSIBLE FOOTBALL GAMBLING.

text.p: Boston College has appointed an internal review committee to investigate allegations that some of its football players bet on college football games, possibly including their own, the school confirmed Monday.

Kevin P. Duffy, vice president for student affairs, will head the internal review committee, which will also include Wayne Budd, a former United States attorney for Massachusetts. The school has also notified the NCAA that it is looking into the allegations.
Boston College plays at home this Saturday against Notre Dame.

"This is a very public issue and I'm concerned about the health and welfare of our players and coaches," head coach Dan Henning said Monday. "We hope this situation can come to a swift conclusion and we can get on and play football."
Henning said he has not been given a time frame as to when the investigation would be completed.

The coach said no players have been suspended for Saturday's game, other than junior wideout Steve Everson, who was suspended indefinitely from the team for refusing to enter last Thursday's game against Pittsburgh.

Boston College athletic director Chet Gladchuk confirmed at a news conference Saturday night that Boston College police and the Middlesex County District Attorney's office are investigating allegations into gambling.

Gladchuk said that Henning heard after an October 26 loss to Syracuse that some of his players may have bet on college football games. Gladchuk said the allegations became strong enough to warrant an investigation.
The Eagles were 11 1/2 point favourites against Pittsburgh last Thursday, but lost 20-13.

Boston College was the centre of a previous gambling investigation. Basketball player Rick Kuhn was sentenced to 10 years in a federal prison for conspiring to fix six games during the 1978-79 season.
